statement: The function returns a result r such that len(r) = n - k + 1, and for every i with 0 <= i < n - k + 1: let W_i be the multiset of entries nums[j] with i <= j < i+k. For each integer v let f_i(v) be the number of occurrences of v in W_i, and let D_i = {v | f_i(v) > 0}. Then r[i] = sum_{v in S_i} v * f_i(v), where S_i is the unique subset of D_i with |S_i| = min(x, |D_i|) such that for every u in S_i and every v in D_i \ S_i, either f_i(u) > f_i(v), or f_i(u) = f_i(v) and u > v. Equivalently, S_i consists of the min(x, |D_i|) distinct values whose pairs (f_i(v), v) are largest in lexicographic descending order.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000. Interpreting k and x as mathematical integers, 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= k. For every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and len(r) = n - k + 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000. Interpreting k and x as mathematical integers, 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= k. For every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and for every i with 0 <= i < n - k + 1, r[i] >= x (comparing the mathematical integer value of r[i] with the mathematical integer value of x).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000. Interpreting k and x as mathematical integers, 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= k. For every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and for every i with 0 <= i < n - k + 1, r[i] <= sum_{j=i}^{i+k-1} nums[j]. That is, the x-sum of a window never exceeds the ordinary sum of all entries in that window.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000. Interpreting k and x as mathematical integers, 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= k. For every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r; in particular, under the stated constraints it does not fail, panic, access out of bounds, or overflow in computing lengths, frequencies, or sums.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000. Interpreting k and x as mathematical integers, 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= k. For every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r such that len(r) = n and for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] = nums[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000. Interpreting k and x as mathematical integers, 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= k. For every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000. Also k = 1.

statement: The function returns a result r and for every i with 0 <= i < n - k + 1: let W_i be the multiset of entries nums[j] with i <= j < i+k and let f_i(v) be the number of occurrences of v in W_i. If v_i is a value occurring in W_i that maximizes the pair (f_i(v), v) in lexicographic descending order, then r[i] = v_i * f_i(v_i).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000. Interpreting k and x as mathematical integers, 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= k. For every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000. Also x = 1.

statement: The function returns a result r and for every i with 0 <= i < n - k + 1, if the k entries of the window nums[i..i+k-1] are pairwise distinct, then r[i] equals the sum of the x largest values in that window (if x = k this is the sum of all k entries).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000. Interpreting k and x as mathematical integers, 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= k. For every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and for every i with 0 <= i < n - k + 1, if the number of distinct values occurring in nums[i..i+k-1] is at most x, then r[i] = sum_{j=i}^{i+k-1} nums[j].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000. Interpreting k and x as mathematical integers, 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= k. For every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let r1 = find_x_sum(nums, k, x1) and r2 = find_x_sum(nums, k, x2). Both calls return results, len(r1) = len(r2) = n - k + 1, and for every i with 0 <= i < n - k + 1, r1[i] <= r2[i] (as mathematical integers).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000. Interpreting x1, x2, and k as mathematical integers, 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x1 <= x2 <= k. For every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let r = find_x_sum(nums, k, x), let nums2 be the slice with nums2[j] = c * nums[j] for every j, and let r2 = find_x_sum(nums2, k, x). Both calls return results, len(r2) = len(r) = n - k + 1, and for every i with 0 <= i < n - k + 1, r2[i] = c * r[i] (as mathematical integers).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000. Interpreting k and x as mathematical integers, 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= k. For every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000. Let c be a positive integer such that 1 <= c * nums[j] <= 1000000000 for every j with 0 <= j < n.

statement: Let r = find_x_sum(nums, k, x) and r2 = find_x_sum(nums2, k, x). Both calls return results, and for every i with 0 <= i < n - k + 1, if the multiset of entries nums[i..i+k-1] equals the multiset of entries nums2[i..i+k-1], then r[i] = r2[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000. Interpreting k and x as mathematical integers, 1 <= k <= n and 1 <= x <= k. For every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000. Let nums2 be another slice with len(nums2) = n and 1 <= nums2[j] <= 1000000000 for every j with 0 <= j < n.

statement: Let r = find_x_sum(nums,k,x) and r2 = find_x_sum(nums2,k,x). Both return results with len r = len r2 = n-k+1, and for every i with 0 <= i < n-k+1, r2[i] = r[n-k-i] (reversing the input reverses the answer).
preconditions: Let n=len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n, 1 <= x <= k, 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000 for all j; let nums2 be defined by nums2[j] = nums[n-1-j] for 0 <= j < n (so nums2 is also a valid input).

statement: The function returns a result r and, for every i with 0 <= i < n-k+1, r[i] = sum_{j=i}^{i+k-1} nums[j] if AND ONLY IF the number of distinct values occurring in nums[i..i+k-1] is at most x. (S11 only states the 'if' direction; the converse—when more than x distinct values occur at least one positive value is dropped, so the sum is strictly smaller—is the missing part.)
preconditions: Let n=len(nums). 1 <= n <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n, 1 <= x <= k, and 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000000 for all j.

statement: Let K_i(x) be the set of distinct values kept from nums[i..i+k-1] when the parameter is x. For every i with 0 <= i < n-k+1, K_i(x1) is a subset of K_i(x2) (the kept-value sets are nested in x); consequently r1[i] <= r2[i] (this strict set-nesting strengthens the sum-monotonicity of spec_10).
